source.title: Resisting Harmful Instructions through Training-Free Weight Editing
source.authors: Ali Ebrahimpour-Boroojeny; Xiao-Cong Yang; Samuel Schapiro; Z. Borhani; Francisco R. Ortega; Yu-Jia Zheng; Cheng-Xiang Zhai

page_placements.theme: Analogues: contrastive single directions for other behaviours and concepts (not refusal)

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses difference-in-means activation steering (CAA) as a baseline and also ablates format-specific CAA directions, but its measured behavior is compliance with orders to lie, not refusal of harmful user requests. It does not test the refusal direction or the claim’s refusal outcomes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for CAA steering and for projecting CAA directions out of every layer in a format-transfer study. These measure honesty under orders to lie, a related but different behavior from refusal. The paper’s weight-editing results concern a distinct intervention, not the single residual-stream refusal direction. No cited results from other work are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper's behaviour is honesty and fairness under operator orders to lie or be sexist. It does not measure refusal of harmful requests, and it never extracts or ablates a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. Difference-in-means CAA appears only as a baseline to the authors' weight-editing method. Appendix H borrows the Arditi et al. ablation procedure, but applies it to a lie-versus-truth direction. The refusal direction is cited only in passing (Appendix A.3) to explain why the edit acts at intermediate depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that graded activation-contrast weight edits reduce compliance with instructed lying and sexism and beat CAA on single-turn format transfer. They also report costs to capability, selectivity, language transfer and multi-turn settings. They draw no conclusion about the refusal direction.
record.recipe_differences: The main intervention edits selected weights using contrastive channel activations, rather than ablating or adding a single residual-stream refusal direction. CAA based on difference-in-means vectors is used as a baseline; the format-study ablation removes a lie-related CAA direction, not a refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity of its lie-related results to prompt family, editing strength, language, and evaluation format; these do not establish sensitivity of the claimed refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: A difference-in-means lie-versus-truth direction, added at one layer, raises honest rates under orders to lie on most models (e.g. Llama 31.0%→83.3%). Projecting it out of every layer has mixed effects across formats: −19 to +20 points, and rates fall on Falcon.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means directions for instructed lying mediate compliance with lie orders, with effects that depend on model and prompt format.

record.problems: No refusal-specific intervention or refusal outcome is tested. The all-layer direction-ablation results are summarized as ranges across formats, and the paper notes that the format study does not isolate weight space versus activation space as the source of differences. General capability costs are reported for the paper’s weight edits, not for a refusal-direction ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows. The many weight-edit results, sexism outcomes, capability results, and attack/transfer evaluations concern the paper’s distinct weight-edit method and do not measure the refusal direction or refusal behavior.

untested.parts: No harmful-versus-harmless direction; no refusal ablation or addition; no refusal rate.
No abliteration. The weight edit targets lying and sexism, not refusal.
The attacks (translated orders, many-shot lies) target lie orders; there is no refusal-direction suppression and no adversarial training.
Harmfulness judgment is not separated from refusal.
Language transfer is measured for lie edits only, not for a refusal direction.
No comparison of training procedures or stages.

record.verdict_notes: The refusal-direction paper (Arditi et al.) is cited only for the ablation method and the intermediate-layer location. The edited sexism models seldom refuse: the edit corrects or answers fairly rather than refusing. No row bears on any version, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal-direction ablation or addition is tested; no refusal rate or general capability outcome under such an intervention is measured.
The paper edits weights using activation contrasts for lying and sexism, not an ablation of the refusal direction; it does not test released-model abliteration.
The attacks change the wording or context of orders to lie; they do not suppress the refusal direction or test training against its ablation.
No claim about the geometry or number of refusal directions is tested.
The paper does not measure harmfulness judgment separately from refusal.
It tests transfer of its weight edits and lie-related CAA across formats and some languages, not transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or training stages.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or stages is reported.
No reasoning-model test of the refusal direction is reported.

unmatched_labels.label: none
unmatched_labels.reason: No version is tested: no refusal measure and no harmful-minus-harmless direction. The lie-direction ablation fits no version.

relation.reason: Applies the Arditi et al. projection-out-of-every-layer technique to a lie-vs-truth CAA direction (Appendix H) as a comparator. Elsewhere it only cites or discusses the refusal direction (Related work; Appendix A.3, intermediate-layer extraction).

tranche.reason: Measures honesty and sexism under operator orders, not refusal of harmful requests. Uses DIM CAA and Arditi-style all-layer directional ablation (on a lie-vs-truth direction) only as baselines to its own weight edit. No harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction is extracted or tested.

source_check.notes: Table 1 contradicts itself. Its average row is not the mean of its per-model cells (e.g. CAA LIARS' BENCH cells average 78.1, stated 78.7; AI Liar 78.0 vs 74.8). The OLMo row's AI Liar lead does not compute (1.5 vs the stated +0.5). The OLMo model is labelled 7B in Table 1 but 1B in Table 12 ('Settings behind Table 1'). The authors_conclusion paraphrase is accurate.

statements.correction: CAA added at one layer (Table 1, 25+25 prompts): LIARS' BENCH honest rate rises on all 5 models (Llama 31.0 to 83.3, Phi 68.4 to 78.1, Falcon 80.9 to 84.2, OLMo 51.1 to 53.8, Qwen2.5-3B 81.7 to 91.1). AI Liar rises on 4 of 5 (Falcon 73.3 to 72.4). Projecting the format-specific CAA direction out of every layer (Appendix H, 200 pairs per format): Phi -1 to +15, Llama +2 to +20, Qwen2.5-7B -19 to +15 points; Falcon decreases, size not stated. Authors: less effective than either primary intervention.
statements.problem: The numbers are right. But the -19 to +20 range covers only Phi, Llama and Qwen2.5-7B: Falcon also falls, by an amount the paper doesn't state. Also, 'it' merges two different directions: the projected-out one is the format study's per-format 200-pair CAA direction (4 models), not the 25-prompt single-layer Table 1 vector (5 models).
